card.name: Farandole
card.era: Name attested from the 18th c.; practiced earlier
card.tagline: Open-chain community dance of Provence led by a leader.
card.profile: The farandole is an open-chain community dance of Provence in 6/8 time, in which dancers join hands (or link by handkerchief/ribbon) in a long line led by a leader who waves a flag and guides the chain through spirals, serpentines and arches (Wikipedia; Britannica). It is accompanied by the galoubet (a three-holed pipe) and the tambourin (a long Provencal tabor), both played by a single tambourinaire. Danced at major Provencal feasts (Corpus Christi; Tarascon's Tarasque festival) and embedded in the Provencal Christmas creche tradition. It resembles the gavotte, jig and tarantella; the Revolutionary carmagnole is a derivative.
card.insight: Bizet used a Provencal farandole tune in the finale of his 'L'Arlesienne' Suite No. 2 (arr. Guiraud, 1879), helping popularize the form in classical music (Encyclopedia.com / Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music).
card.image_significance: Serpentine open-chain community dance. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Provence, France.
